title: Uniaxial tension of a J2 bilinear-hardening cube to large strain (implicit, finite strain)
source: J2 plasticity with linear isotropic hardening in uniaxial stress (Simo and Hughes, Computational Inelasticity, Springer 1998, §2.3) in the logarithmic strain, which Simo's exponential return map (CMAME 99:61–112, 1992) integrates exactly on a proportional path: Kirchhoff stress τ = σ_y + E_t (ε − σ_y/E), Cauchy stress σ = τ/J with ln J = τ/(3K) (Hencky's volume law)

quantities.quantity: axial Cauchy stress at a logarithmic strain of 0.2
quantities.reason: a homogeneous deformation the element represents exactly, reached on a proportional path: the tolerance only admits the Newton tolerance and rounding
ε_p = (τ − σ_y)/H, as for the stress
